legacy_cells.C: Wilasinee Samniang; Syed Muhammad Tariq Shah; Yin May Tun; Adeel Munawar; Sarin KC
legacy_cells.I: 042_2026_A hybrid grey wolf optimized eXtreme gradient boosting-based machine learning model for hospital pharmaceutical demand forecasting.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Weekly pharmaceutical demand for medicines dispensed at two provincial hospitals
legacy_cells.S: What will weekly hospital demand be for medicines, using dispensing, temporal, and meteorological data?
legacy_cells.T: Operational data from Pasang Hospital and Banthi Hospital in Lamphun Province, Thailand, covering October 2023–May 2025
legacy_cells.U: Hospital managers and personnel responsible for procurement and inventory planning
legacy_cells.V: Inform pharmaceutical procurement, purchase orders, and inventory planning
legacy_cells.DN: Pasang Hospital and Banthi Hospital dispensing records with localized Open-Meteo weather data
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes a hybrid Grey Wolf Optimizer–XGBoost model for hospital pharmaceutical-demand forecasting, using dispensing, temporal, and weather features and benchmarking against five machine-learning baselines.
legacy_cells.FN: Proposed model: MAE 0.81, RMSE 2.65, R2 0.984, reported as best among the compared models.
legacy_cells.FO: Validation used two provincial hospitals over a relatively short observation period; the authors describe the findings as proof of concept and call for broader external validation.
legacy_cells.FP: Expand data coverage across regions and hospital tiers, externally validate at new hospitals, incorporate additional demand drivers, explore recurrent and graph neural networks, and integrate with hospital information systems and national supply-chain platforms.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify limited hospital-level forecasting, particularly in lower- and middle-income settings, and few studies incorporating environmental and temporal factors.
legacy_cells.FR: This is a tabular demand forecaster, not a patient/procedure/system state-transition model: reported methods map selected predictors to weekly demand, and operational decision-support integration is described as beyond scope. No learned state evolution, action-conditioned rollouts, counterfactual identification, or planner results are demonstrated.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pages 1–16: title and abstract; introduction and literature review; methods (study setting/data sources, preprocessing, optimization, model training, decision-support discussion, and metrics); results and Tables 1–5 plus relevant figures; discussion and stated limitations; conclusion; code/data availability and ethics statements. Full extracted text reviewed throughout; no unreadable tables noted. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I left unchanged. Paper is an empirical demand-forecasting study but does not define or evaluate a persistent state-transition world model; forecast-to-procurement integration is conceptual and the authors call the work proof of concept. DV=No reflects internal temporal holdout only; external validation is explicitly deferred. Evidence QA: 30/36 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (83.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 33 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 3 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All16physical pages/46references read; all8figures5tables visually inspected p3–5,8–13. All pages rendered; no included appendix.
Forecast lead/lag feature construction, future-weather availability, target transformation/backtransformation and physical medicine demand units unresolved; no recursive/persistent state documented.
Figure1 GWO feature selection precedes splitting; scope of preprocessing/selection/CV fit relative heldout test unreported. This is leakage uncertainty, not demonstrated contamination.
Literature R2 Figure7 combines different tasks/data (drug response/prices/demand); cannot establish across-study superiority/generalization. Internal twohospital pool not external validation.
Procurement/stockout/wastage improvement untested; recommendations not implemented workflow. Code DOI not retrieved. Single-model source review, no independent human review or replication.
notes: GWO iteration/boosting round not health-system time. Figures6 tenweek traces are diagnostic temporal plots, not proven recursive tenstep rollout or effective horizon. Low SD across seeds not predictive probability calibration. R2independent of non-WM status.
